tagline: Find any file path on any host — and tag where it lives.
lore: The Greyhound, fastest of the hounds — here it sprints through every filesystem path navi has found on your assets.
problem: The paths a scanner finds reveal where software actually lives — a vulnerable library, a copied binary, an app outside the package manager. Finding every host with one path shouldn't need SQL.
does: Greyhound searches the filesystem paths found on assets by path text, with the plugin that found each and the host and IP. Tag applies Path : <name> to every asset carrying that exact path.

glance.caption: Greyhound's results: each path with its plugin, host and IP, and a Tag button per path.

capabilities: by any part of the path.
the plugin, host and IP for each path; the host opens Argos.
Path : <name> on every asset with that exact path, with an editable value, behind the write gate and a confirm.
how: Greyhound reads the filesystem paths in your local navi.db without changing it; results page on the server, 20 rows a page (up to 50). Tags go through navi's tag-by-query.
who: Analysts locating a file or package across hosts, and owners checking where their software is deployed.
better: Cavall turns unnamed paths into Custom App tags, Atlas maps paths to owners, and Wolfhound does the same for application routes.
cta: Type a path — Greyhound finds every host it lives on.
